title: Abba Kohen Bardela
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: Hyman places him among the last of the Tannaim. He is mentioned in [Sifrei Devarim, section 2](https://www.sefaria.org/Sifrei_Devarim.2.2), where Abba Yose ben Hanan teaches in his name (and in [Yalkut Devarim, remez 799](https://www.sefaria.org/Yalkut_Shimoni_on_Torah.799.1), the reading is ben Hananya). In [Bava Metzia 10a](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Metzia.10a.14) and [10b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Metzia.10b.7), Resh Lakish states in his name the well-known law that a person's four cubits acquire for him anywhere, and the law that a minor girl has no courtyard and no four cubits. Hyman infers there that he lived in the time of R' Yannai, the teacher of R' Yohanan, for there R' Yohanan, in the name of R' Yannai, disputes with Resh Lakish, who speaks in the name of Abba Kohen Bardela.

And Hyman cites [Jerusalem Talmud Peah, chapter 4, halakhah 2](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Peah.4.2.3), for R' Shimon ben Lakish stating in his name the law of a person who acquires a found object on behalf of his fellow. In [Jerusalem Talmud Bava Batra, chapter 8, halakhah 3](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Bava_Batra.8.3.2), he states in his name a law of inheritance, and there he is called "Bar Daluyah"; Hyman identifies him as the very same person.

And in Bereshit Rabbah 79:9 as cited by Hyman, “ר״ה” (the name is abbreviated) cites him; and in Shir HaShirim Rabbah 4:14, section 6 as cited by Hyman, R' Avin speaks in the name of R' Abba Kohen ben Dalya. It is impossible to know whether "Bardela" is a personal name or a place name, as we find in [Kilayim, end of chapter 8](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Kilayim.8.4.7), and Terumot 10:7 as cited by Hyman, "R' Yudah ben Pazi, de-Bar Dalya" (supplied ר"י בן פזי), and in [Eruvin, chapter 6, halakhah 8](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Eruvin.6.8.8), "the people of Bardelaya."

notes.text: The consulted editions place the corresponding passages at [Bereshit Rabbah 76:9](https://www.sefaria.org/Bereshit_Rabbah.76.9), with Rav Huna explicitly named, and [Shir HaShirim Rabbah 2:14:6](https://www.sefaria.org/Shir_HaShirim_Rabbah.2.14.6), with Rabbi Avin as the transmitter. These are parallel locators for Hyman’s citations. [Heilprin’s entry on Abba Yose ben Hanan](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=1991&lang=en) also records the Sifrei transmission.

The consulted [Terumot 10:5:2](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Terumot.10.5.2) reads Yudah bar Pazi, de-Bar Dalya. The linked Kilayim reads Yudah ben Pazi. Hyman leaves the personal-versus-place question open. In Peah, the opening statement concerns a finder’s own four cubits. The [later discussion](https://www.sefaria.org/Jerusalem_Talmud_Peah.4.2.7) compares finds and gifts acquired through others.

The consulted Sifrei Devarim 2 names Abba Yose ben Hanan quoting Abba Kohen ben Dalya. Yalkut Shimoni 799 preserves Hananya in parentheses beside Hanan in brackets. Bava Metzia 10a–10b gives both the four-cubit rule and the minor girl’s lack of a courtyard and four cubits, with the stated reporting chains. The opening rule in the consulted Jerusalem Talmud Peah 4:2 passage describes acquiring a find within one’s own four cubits; the following discussion compares the acquisition of finds and gifts through another person. Hyman’s description as acquisition for another remains his abridged account of this discussion, rather than an independently established quotation of its opening rule. Jerusalem Talmud Bava Batra 8:3 names Abba bar Delaiah in an inheritance rule, with Cohen supplied in brackets in the English edition. Hyman’s definite same-person identification is retained as his conclusion. A directly consulted Bereshit Rabbah 76:9 names Rav Huna quoting Rabbi Abba HaKohen Bardela; this is a named alternative locus to the supplied 79:9, not proof of that exact edition or a global expansion of R-H. The Avin–Abba Kohen ben Delaya chain is directly present in Shir HaShirim Rabbah 2:14, section 6, beside Hyman’s supplied chapter 4/on verse 14/section 6. The Hebrew and its abbreviated title remain unchanged. The Terumot witness’s Yudah bar Pazi beside supplied ben Pazi and its 10:5 location beside 10:7 remain distinct. None of these forms settles the personal-name-versus-place question, admits a town identity, or independently establishes Hyman’s chronology.
